sentences.text: Researchers developed a 2D U-Net, a computer program designed to automatically identify and measure specific brain parts, stroke damage, and tumors in rats. The model was evaluated across three specific tasks: mapping healthy brain areas, detecting stroke lesions, and locating brain tumors.

To verify its performance, the accuracy of the computer's work was checked by comparing its results to manual measurements and previous computer models. After the researchers fixed a data error that would have allowed the computer to cheat, the model performed well on all tasks.
The authors conclude that this new method is superior to older approaches because it is more accurate, functions across different MRI setups, and saves time.
